fixes.explanation: Bowstrings, baker? You walked in with a whole archery shop. The text says the men of Judah bound Samson with two new ropes (Judges 15:13). They'd just promised not to kill him, and ropes were how they kept that promise and still handed him over. Then the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and the ropes on his arms became like burnt flax (Judges 15:14). I bet seven bowstrings wouldn't have lasted any longer.

An altar? That's a holy thought, friend, but nobody in this scene is picking up a hammer. Samson has just struck down a thousand men with a jawbone, and then he casts it from his hand. The text says he names the place Ramath-lehi (Judges 15:17). Next thing he does is cry out to the LORD because he is very thirsty (Judges 15:18). I think a man that parched is looking for water, not building supplies.
